source_text: De his quae a exploratoribus renuntiantur et de indignatione Domini. Populus infidelitatis desperatione praeceps agitur et ad lapidandos eos qui bona nuntiant prosilit; maiestas Domini protegit eos. Dicit Dominus: percutiam eos peste et faciam te in gentem magnam. Fit comminatio non ut passibilis ostendatur divina natura, sed ut Moysi caritas et Dei bonitas innotesceret.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning these which by scouts are-reported and concerning indignation of-Lord. People of-unbelief by-desperation headlong is-driven and toward to-be-stoned those who good-things announce leaps-forth; majesty of-Lord protects them. Says Lord: I-will-strike them with-plague and I-will-make you into nation great. Is-made threat not that passible be-shown divine nature, but that of-Moses love and of-God goodness might-become-known.
pass_b_english: On what the scouts report and on the Lord’s indignation: the people, panic-struck by unbelief, rush to stone those who bring good news, while the Lord’s majesty covers them. The Lord says, [[I will strike them with pestilence and make of you a greater nation >> Bible:Numbers 14:12]]. The threat is written not to show God passible, but that Moses’ love and God’s goodness may be known.
